provenance: ADR-033 §d, the invariant-suite half of S10's acceptance, stated the way boilerplate-offsets-invariant states ADR-026's and tables-offsets-invariant states ADR-029's. INV-S2 says item text is a verbatim slice of normalized_text and that offsets index normalized_text; ADR-033 rules that image references are reported as offsets INTO that text and that the text is never edited to carry them, which makes 'default-flag output is byte-identical before and after' an EQUALITY rather than a promise -- so the check asserts the equality directly: extract_items(path, images=True) and extract_items(path, images=False) on the same file, normalized_text / items / warnings / doc_status (the adapter's DETERMINISM_FIELDS) compared field by field, plus the default-off half in both directions (no `images` key at all without the flag, a list with it). `envelope_shape` here also runs `_images_shape` over every record, so a record that is not in the contract shape is red on this case and not only on one that labels an image. WHY xom-2021 AND NOT jpm-2024. jpm-2024 is the largest fixture and carries the most images (14), and it is where a text-REWRITING implementation would displace the most offsets -- which is the argument tables-offsets-invariant makes for choosing it. Two things move the choice here. First, the scale assertion is already bought elsewhere: jpm-2024-images runs `envelope_shape`/`_images_shape` over all 14 records inside a 1,213,284-char text in the `fast` suite, so nothing about scale is lost by putting the INVARIANT case on a smaller file. Second, the invariant suite is the one the PostToolUse hook runs on every edit, and it already pays 1.3 s for tables-offsets-invariant on jpm-2024; this case on xom-2021 costs 0.28 s + 0.27 s for its two extractions instead of roughly 0.6 s + 0.6 s (measured 2026-08-23). Stated plainly so it is not mistaken for an accident: the cheaper fixture was chosen deliberately, and the reason it is not a weaker assertion is the sentence before this one. What xom-2021 buys that jpm-2024 would not: it is the fixture with three images at ONE offset (g7/g8/g9, all at 232186 -- adjacent elements whose intervening markup collapses to nothing under ADR-003's whitespace canon). Document order for images is therefore non-decreasing and not strictly increasing, and `_images_shape`'s ordering rule has to allow that. A shape check written with `<=` where it needed `<` -- or an implementation that nudged coincident images apart, which would be a text edit by another name -- is red here and nowhere else in the invariant suite. In the invariant suite because a break here is not a quality regression: it is the provenance guarantee INV-S2 exists for, and it is the single clause of the S10 Validation gate ('default-flag output byte-identical before and after') that has to hold on every run rather than once.
